newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq UN envoy sees no problem in resuming oil plan.
newsitem.headline: Iraq UN envoy sees no problem in resuming oil plan.

text.p: Iraq's envoy to the United Nations, Nizar Hamdoon, said he foresees no problem in implementing the final stages of the oil-for-food accord that would allow resumption of the second tranche of Iraqi oil sales under sanctions imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
Hamdoon told Reuters Tuesday that Iraq had formally submitted its aid distribution plan Monday afternoon, quelling talk that he was to formally submit the plan Tuesday.
Hamdoon spoke on his way to a meeting with UN Department of Humanitarian Affairs chief Yasushi Akashi, during which the two will discuss the aid plan approval process.
Iraq has been permitted since June 8, to sell a second round of $2 billion worth of oil, but has insisted that an aid plan be approved before exports resume.
UN Secretary General Kofi Annan and his staff are currently evaluating the Iraqi plan, and most diplomats expect Annan's approval by the end of July.

"I'm confident. Everybody needs money, so I don't foresee any problems," Hamdoon said. He said the UN needs money as much as Iraq, specifically to pay for monitoring operations related to the oil-for-food scheme, and for weapons inspections programs.
Hamdoon also denied that Iraq had submitted a pricing formula, which is a necessary component for resuming the awarding of oil contracts.
